    39	/-! ## Pushforward commutes with the Čech complex functor -/
    40	
    41	/- Planner strategy: lem:pushforward_mapHC_cechComplexOnX ·
    42	Both complexes are built as `alternatingCofaceMapComplex` of the same cosimplicial object, differing
    43	only in whether `f_*` is applied before or after the alternating coface construction.  Since `f_*`
    44	is additive, `(f_*).mapHomologicalComplex` commutes with `alternatingCofaceMapComplex` by the
    45	naturality of `CosimplicialObject.whiskering` and the fact that the alternating-coface differential
    46	is an alternating sum that `f_*` preserves by additivity.
    47	Concretely: `cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F = alternatingCofaceMapComplex.obj (drop (CechNerve 𝒰 F))`,
    48	and `CechComplex f 𝒰 F = relativeCechComplexOfNerve f (CechNerve 𝒰 F)
    49	                        = alternatingCofaceMapComplex.obj (f_* ∘ drop (CechNerve 𝒰 F))`.
    50	The iso is the natural isomorphism between the two functors
    51	`alternatingCofaceMapComplex ∘ whiskering(f_*)` and `(f_*).mapHomologicalComplex ∘ alternatingCofaceMapComplex`
    52	applied to the same cosimplicial object; the components are identities in each degree. -/
    53	/-- **An additive functor commutes with the alternating coface map complex** (object-level
    54	cosimplicial analogue of `AlgebraicTopology.map_alternatingFaceMapComplex`). The components are
    55	identities: in each degree both complexes have the object `G.obj (Y.obj ⦋p⦌)`, and the
    56	differential of the whiskered complex is `G` applied to the alternating coface differential,
    57	by additivity (`Functor.map_sum`, `Functor.map_zsmul`). Project-local helper. -/
    58	noncomputable def mapAlternatingCofaceMapComplexIso
    59	    {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Preadditive C] [Preadditive D]
    60	    (G : C ⥤ D) [G.Additive] (Y : CosimplicialObject C) :
    61	    (G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
    62	        ((AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex C).obj Y) ≅
    63	      (AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex D).obj
    64	        (((CosimplicialObject.whiskering C D).obj G).obj Y) :=
    65	  HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents (fun _ => Iso.refl _) (by
    66	    rintro i j (rfl : i + 1 = j)
    67	    -- (v4.31.0: `dsimp only [AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.obj]` no longer reduces the functor-
    68	    -- wrapped `.obj`, so the old `dsimp; rw [of_d]` broke. Unfold the functor + def + `of_d`
    69	    -- via `simp only`, clear the (defeq-wrapped) identity components with `erw`, then both sides
    70	    -- are the alternating sum `∑ (-1)^k • G.map (Y.δ k)` definitionally — `(whisker G Y).δ` is
    71	    -- `rfl`-equal to `G.map (Y.δ)` — so `rfl` closes it.)
    72	    simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Functor.mapHomologicalComplex_obj_d,
    73	      AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex,
    74	      AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.obj, CochainComplex.of_d,
    75	      AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingCofaceMapComplex.objD, Functor.map_sum, Functor.map_zsmul]
    76	    erw [Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]
    77	    rfl)
    78	
    79	/-- **The `f_*`-image of the un-augmented Čech complex on `X` is isomorphic to the relative Čech
    80	complex** (blueprint `lem:pushforward_mapHC_cechComplexOnX`). -/
    81	noncomputable def pushforward_mapHomologicalComplex_cechComplexOnX
    82	    (f : X ⟶ S) (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules) :
    83	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
    84	        (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F) ≅ CechComplex f 𝒰 F :=
    85	  -- `cechComplexOnX` and `CechComplex` are *definitionally* the alternating coface complexes of
    86	  -- the (un-whiskered, resp. `f_*`-whiskered) underlying cosimplicial object of the Čech nerve,
    87	  -- so the general helper applies on the nose.
    88	  mapAlternatingCofaceMapComplexIso (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f)
    89	    (CosimplicialObject.Augmented.drop.obj (CechNerve 𝒰 F))
    90	
    91	/-! ## From augmented exactness to the acyclic-resolution input data -/
    92	
    93	/- Planner strategy: lem:cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput ·
    94	From `cechAugmented_exact` (CechAugmentedResolution.lean) we have:
    95	  `∀ p, IsZero ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).homology p)`.
    96	The augmented complex has `X 0 = F` and `X (n+1) = (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).X n`; its differential at
    97	degree 0 is the augmentation `ε : F → C⁰`.
    98	
    99	(1) Exactness of `cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F` at degree `n+1`:  the augmented complex at degree `n+2`
   100	    coincides with the un-augmented complex at degree `n+1`.  Use
   101	    `HomologicalComplex.exactAt_iff_isZero_homology` plus the vanishing from `cechAugmented_exact`.
   102	
   103	(2) Iso `e : F ≅ (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).cycles 0`:  vanishing of homology at degree 0 gives that
   104	    ε is a monomorphism; vanishing at degree 1 gives that the image of ε equals `ker d⁰ = cycles 0`.
   105	    Hence ε is an iso onto `cycles 0`.  The iso is assembled from the augmentation `cechAugmentation`
   106	    and the exactness data; use `ShortComplex.Exact.isoOfEpiMonoIsZero` or similar.
   107	
   108	Both outputs are assembled into a `PProd` (anonymous constructor `⟨e, hexact⟩`; `PProd` rather
   109	than `Prod` because the second component is a `Prop` while the first is an `Iso` in `Type`). -/
   110	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   111	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
   112	-- Normalizing the cover-indexed degree shifts below exceeds 1,600,000 heartbeats in `whnf`.
   113	/-- **From augmented exactness to the P4 input data**
   114	(blueprint `lem:cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput`).
   115	
   116	Given the hypotheses of `cechAugmented_exact`, this declaration packages the two pieces of data
   117	that `rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution` (the abstract acyclic-resolution lemma) requires:
   118	an isomorphism `e : F ≅ (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).cycles 0` identifying `F` with the 0-cocycles,
   119	and exactness `(cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).ExactAt (n+1)` in every positive degree. -/
   120	noncomputable def cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput
   121	    (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)) [X.IsSeparated]
   122	    (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) :
   123	    (F ≅ (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).cycles 0) ×' (∀ n, (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).ExactAt (n + 1)) := by
   124	  have hKex : ∀ p, (cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).ExactAt p := fun p =>
   125	    (HomologicalComplex.exactAt_iff_isZero_homology _ p).2 (cechAugmented_exact 𝒰 h𝒰 F hF p)
   126	  -- (1) positive-degree exactness: sc' of augmented at (n+2) = sc' of original at (n+1)
   127	  -- because CochainComplex.augment_X_succ and augment_d_succ_succ are both rfl.
   128	  -- Explicit have-steps with fully-typed RHS prevent whnf elaboration blowup.
   129	  have hexact : ∀ n, (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).ExactAt (n + 1) := by
   130	    intro n
   131	    have h : (cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).ExactAt (n + 2) := hKex (n + 2)
   132	    have h' : ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).sc' (n + 1) (n + 2) (n + 3)).Exact :=
   133	      ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).exactAt_iff' (n + 1) (n + 2) (n + 3)
   134	        ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).prev_eq' rfl) ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).next_eq' rfl)).mp h
   135	    have h'' : ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).sc' n (n + 1) (n + 2)).Exact := h'
   136	    exact ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).exactAt_iff' n (n + 1) (n + 2)
   137	      ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).prev_eq' rfl) ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).next_eq' rfl)).mpr h''
   138	  -- (2) exactness at degree 0 gives Mono (cechAugmentation).
   139	  have h0 : (cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).ExactAt 0 := hKex 0
   140	  have h0' : ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).sc' 0 0 1).Exact :=
   141	    ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).exactAt_iff' 0 0 1 CochainComplex.prev_nat_zero
   142	      ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).next_eq' rfl)).mp h0
   143	  haveI hmono : Mono (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F) :=
   144	    h0'.mono_g ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).shape 0 0 (by simp))
   145	  -- (3) exactness at degree 1 gives the lift for the inverse iso.
   146	  have h1 : (cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).ExactAt 1 := hKex 1
   147	  have h1' : ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).sc' 0 1 2).Exact :=
   148	    ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).exactAt_iff' 0 1 2
   149	      ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).prev_eq' rfl) ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).next_eq' rfl)).mp h1
   150	  haveI : Mono ((cechAugmentedComplex 𝒰 F).sc' 0 1 2).f := hmono
   151	  -- Bind both maps once: otherwise the elided `lift`/`liftCycles` proof-args get distinct
   152	  -- def-eq casts and `rw [HomologicalComplex.liftCycles_i]` grinds at `whnf` on the cover-built
   153	  -- complex (the original `rw`-chains here both fail / time out).
   154	  set inv := h1'.lift ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles 0) ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles_d 0 1)
   155	    with hinv
   156	  set hom := (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).liftCycles (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F) 1
   157	      ((ComplexShape.up ℕ).next_eq' rfl) (cechAugmentation_comp_d 𝒰 F) with hhom
   158	  have hl : inv ≫ cechAugmentation 𝒰 F = (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles 0 := h1'.lift_f _ _
   159	  have hli : hom ≫ (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles 0 = cechAugmentation 𝒰 F :=
   160	    (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).liftCycles_i _ _ _ _
   161	  refine ⟨⟨hom, inv, ?_, ?_⟩, hexact⟩
   162	  · -- hom_inv_id (term-mode: the `≫` def-eq cast between `(sc' …).X₁` and `F` blocks `rw`/`simp`)
   163	    exact (cancel_mono (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)).1
   164	      (((Category.assoc hom inv (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)).trans
   165	          ((congrArg (fun x => hom ≫ x) hl).trans hli)).trans
   166	        (Category.id_comp (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)).symm)
   167	  · -- inv_hom_id
   168	    exact (cancel_mono ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles 0)).1
   169	      (((Category.assoc inv hom ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles 0)).trans
   170	          ((congrArg (fun x => inv ≫ x) hli).trans hl)).trans
   171	        (Category.id_comp ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).iCycles 0)).symm)
   172	/-! ## Capstone: Čech computes higher direct images (affine-cover form) -/
   173	
   174	/- Planner strategy: lem:cech_computes_cohomology ·
   175	Assembly of the four Route-A ingredients:
   176	
   177	(a) `cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput` yields:
   178	    · `e : F ≅ (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).cycles 0`
   179	    · `hexact : ∀ n, (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).ExactAt (n+1)`
   180	
   181	(b) `cechTerm_pushforward_acyclic` provides the typeclass instance:
   182	    `[∀ p, (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).IsRightAcyclic ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).X p)]`
   183	    (introduce with `haveI` for each `p`; or use `inferInstance` if the `∀ p` form is
   184	    synthesisable from a blanket instance).
   185	
   186	(c) `Functor.rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution` (AcyclicResolution.lean, fully proved) with
   187	    G = `Scheme.Modules.pushforward f`, K = `cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F`, A = F, gives:
   188	    `((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F
   189	      ≅ ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F)).homology i`
   190	
   191	(d) `pushforward_mapHomologicalComplex_cechComplexOnX` rewrites the right-hand side to
   192	    `(CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i`.
   193	
   194	The final iso `(CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i ≅ higherDirectImage f i F` is the composite of
   195	(d).symm, (c).symm, noting `higherDirectImage f i F = ((pushforward f).rightDerived i).obj F`.
   196	Wrap in `Nonempty` via `⟨iso⟩`.
   197	
   198	Additive / PreservesFiniteLimits hypotheses on `pushforward f`: `Additive` is an instance;
   199	`PreservesFiniteLimits` is needed for `rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution` (via
   200	`PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f)` — left-exact since it is a right adjoint
   201	via the global sections adjunction). -/
   202	/-- **The Čech complex computes the higher direct images** (Stacks Tag 02KE;
   203	blueprint `lem:cech_computes_cohomology`).
   204	
   205	Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a separated quasi-compact morphism with `X` and `S` both separated, `F` a
   206	quasi-coherent `O_X`-module, `𝒰` a finite affine open cover of `X` (with all cover opens affine,
   207	`h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i)`, so all intersections are affine by `X.IsSeparated`), and `hres`
   208	threading `HasInjectiveResolutions` on each intersection subscheme.  Then for every `i ≥ 0`
   209	there is an isomorphism between the `i`-th cohomology of the relative Čech complex and the `i`-th
   210	higher direct image:
   211	```
   212	  (CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i ≅ R^i f_* F  =  higherDirectImage f i F.
   213	```
   214	This is the canonical statement of the Čech-to-derived-pushforward comparison, proved under the
   215	correct hypotheses `[X.IsSeparated] [S.IsSeparated]` and `h𝒰`. -/
   216	theorem cech_computes_higherDirectImage [HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules]
   217	    (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [X.IsSeparated] [S.IsSeparated]
   218	    (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsAffine (𝒰.X i))
   219	    (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (i : ℕ)
   220	    (hres : ∀ (n : ℕ) (σ : Fin (n + 1) → 𝒰.I₀),
   221	      HasInjectiveResolutions (Scheme.Opens.toScheme (coverInterOpen 𝒰 σ)).Modules) :
   222	    Nonempty ((CechComplex f 𝒰 F).homology i ≅ higherDirectImage f i F) := by
   223	  -- (a) the resolution data extracted from the exactness of the augmented Čech complex
   224	  obtain ⟨e, hexact⟩ := cechAugmented_to_acyclicResolutionInput 𝒰 h𝒰 F hF
   225	  -- (b) termwise right-`f_*`-acyclicity of the Čech complex on `X` (black box from
   226	  -- `CechTermAcyclic.lean`)
   227	  haveI : ∀ n, (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).IsRightAcyclic ((cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F).X n) :=
   228	    fun n => cechTerm_pushforward_acyclic f 𝒰 h𝒰 F hF n (hres n)
   229	  -- (c) `f_*` is left exact: it is a right adjoint (of the module pullback)
   230	  haveI : PreservesLimits (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f) :=
   231	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).rightAdjoint_preservesLimits
   232	  -- (d) assemble: P4 acyclic-resolution comparison, then rewrite `f_* C•` to the relative
   233	  -- Čech complex; `higherDirectImage f i F` is definitionally `((f_*).rightDerived i).obj F`.
   234	  exact ⟨(HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor S.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℕ) i).mapIso
   235	      (pushforward_mapHomologicalComplex_cechComplexOnX f 𝒰 F).symm ≪≫
   236	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution
   237	      (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F) F e hexact i).symm⟩
   238	
   239	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	# Acyclic resolutions compute right-derived functors
    10	
    11	This file provides the abstract homological-algebra core underlying the Čech
    12	computation of higher direct images (Stacks Tag 015E, Leray's acyclicity lemma):
    13	**an acyclic resolution computes every right-derived functor**.
    14	
    15	Throughout, `𝒜` and `ℬ` are abelian categories, `𝒜` has injective resolutions
    16	(so that `G.rightDerived n` is everywhere defined), and `G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` is an
    17	additive functor.
    18	
    19	## Declarations
    20	
    21	* `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightAcyclic` — typeclass for right-`G`-acyclic objects.
    22	* Instance: every injective object is right-acyclic (from Mathlib's

    64	
    65	Given a morphism `φ : S₁ ⟶ S₂` between two short exact sequences of homological complexes
    66	in an abelian category, Mathlib proves that if `φ.τ₁` and `φ.τ₂` are quasi-isomorphisms then so
    67	is `φ.τ₃` (`HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.quasiIso_τ₃`). The companion statements for `φ.τ₁`
    68	and `φ.τ₂` are an explicit Mathlib TODO (see `HomologySequenceLemmas.lean`). We supply the `φ.τ₂`
    69	version here: it is the engine that proves the horseshoe middle complex `I_B` is an injective
    70	*resolution* of `B` (the outer verticals `I_A.ι`, `I_C.ι` are quasi-isos, hence so is the middle
    71	augmentation). The proof mirrors Mathlib's `τ₃` argument: a homology four-lemma on the windows of
    72	`composableArrows₅`, with the boundary degrees (no predecessor / no successor) handled by
    73	`mono_homologyMap_of_mono_of_not_rel` / `epi_homologyMap_of_epi_of_not_rel`. -/

    99	  have hE3 : ∀ d, Epi (homologyMap φ.τ₃ d) := fun d => have := hI3 d; inferInstance

   112	      · exact hE3 i
   113	      · exact hM1 j

   121	        ((δ₀Functor ⋙ δ₀Functor).map (mapComposableArrows₅ φ hS₁ hS₂ k i hki))

   140	### Right-acyclic objects
   141	Blueprint: `def:right_acyclic` (§ "Right-acyclic objects").
   142	-/
   143	
   144	/-- An object `J : 𝒜` is *right-`G`-acyclic* when every higher right-derived
   145	functor of `G` vanishes at `J`:
   146	```
   147	(Rᵏ⁺¹ G)(J) = 0   for all k : ℕ.
   148	```
   149	The index-shifted quantifier `k + 1` matches the statement of
   150	`Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ` and avoids an inequality
   151	side-condition; it is equivalent to `(Rⁿ G)(J) = 0` for all `n ≥ 1`.
   152	
   153	Blueprint: `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightAcyclic` (`def:right_acyclic`).
   154	-/
   155	class Functor.IsRightAcyclic (G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) [G.Additive] (J : 𝒜) : Prop where
   156	  vanish : ∀ k : ℕ, Limits.IsZero ((G.rightDerived (k + 1)).obj J)
   157	
   158	/-- Every injective object is right-`G`-acyclic.
   159	Follows immediately from `Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ`. -/
   160	instance (priority := 100) Functor.IsRightAcyclic.ofInjective
   161	    (G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) [G.Additive] (J : 𝒜) [Injective J] : Functor.IsRightAcyclic G J where
   162	  vanish k := Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ G k J
   163	-- Note: `Functor.isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ` returns
   164	-- `Limits.IsZero ((G.rightDerived (k+1)).obj J)`, matching the class field.

   175	object `J` vanishes in every positive degree. This is the homology-level form of
   176	right-acyclicity, obtained by transporting the vanishing of `(R^{k+1} G)(J)` across
   177	`InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj`. It is the input that kills the middle terms
   178	of the homology long exact sequence in the dimension-shift step. -/
   179	lemma Functor.isZero_homology_mapHomologicalComplex_of_isRightAcyclic

   181	    [G.IsRightAcyclic J] (k : ℕ) :

   184	  (Functor.IsRightAcyclic.vanish (G := G) (J := J) k).of_iso

   204	lemma shortExact_map_mapHomologicalComplex_of_degreewise_splitting

   206	    (splits : ∀ n, (S.map (HomologicalComplex.eval 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).Splitting)

   209	  HomologicalComplex.shortExact_of_degreewise_shortExact _
   210	    (fun n => ((splits n).map G).shortExact)
   211	
   212	/-- **Dimension shift, part (1), from a degreewise-split SES of injective resolutions.**
   213	Given a short exact sequence `0 → A → J → Z → 0` lifted (via the horseshoe) to a
   214	degreewise-split short exact sequence of injective resolutions
   215	`0 → I_A → I_J → I_Z → 0`, presented here as chain maps `φ, ψ` with degreewise splittings,
   216	and with the middle object `J` right-`G`-acyclic, the connecting map of the homology long
   217	exact sequence of `G(I_•)` is an isomorphism in every positive degree:
   218	`(R^{k+1} G)(Z) ≅ (R^{k+2} G)(A)`.
   219	
   220	This is the engine of the staircase induction (`rightDerivedIsoOfAcyclicResolution`).
   221	It is stated over the *resolution-level* SES because the object-level dimension-shift theorem
   222	`rightDerivedShiftIsoOfAcyclic` requires the horseshoe lift to produce that SES; once the
   223	horseshoe is available, the object-level statement follows by feeding its output here. -/
   224	noncomputable def Functor.rightDerivedShiftIsoOfSplitResolutionSES
   225	    (G : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) [G.Additive] {A J Z : 𝒜}
   226	    (I_A : InjectiveResolution A) (I_J : InjectiveResolution J) (I_Z : InjectiveResolution Z)
   227	    [G.IsRightAcyclic J]
   228	    (φ : I_A.cocomplex ⟶ I_J.cocomplex) (ψ : I_J.cocomplex ⟶ I_Z.cocomplex)
   229	    (w : φ ≫ ψ = 0)
   230	    (splits : ∀ n, ((ShortComplex.mk φ ψ w).map
   231	      (HomologicalComplex.eval 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n)).Splitting)
   232	    (k : ℕ) :
   233	    (G.rightDerived (k + 1)).obj Z ≅ (G.rightDerived (k + 2)).obj A :=
   234	  have hSG : ((ShortComplex.mk φ ψ w).map
   235	      (G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ))).ShortExact :=
   236	    shortExact_map_mapHomologicalComplex_of_degreewise_splitting splits G
   237	  (I_Z.isoRightDerivedObj G (k + 1)) ≪≫
   238	    hSG.δIso (k + 1) (k + 2) (by simp)
   239	      (G.isZero_homology_mapHomologicalComplex_of_isRightAcyclic I_J k)
   240	      (G.isZero_homology_mapHomologicalComplex_of_isRightAcyclic I_J (k + 1)) ≪≫
   241	    (I_A.isoRightDerivedObj G (k + 2)).symm
   242

   244	/-- **Horseshoe per-stage monomorphism.** Given an exact short complex
   245	`A → B → C` with `A → B` a monomorphism, and monomorphisms `α : A ↪ P`, `γ : C ↪ Q` with `P`
   246	injective, the map `B → P ⊞ Q` whose first component is the injective extension of `α` along
   247	`A ↪ B` (`Injective.factorThru α S.f`) and whose second component is `B ↠ C ↪ Q` is itself a
   248	monomorphism. This is the cokernel/kernel step driving each stage of the dual Horseshoe Lemma
   249	`InjectiveResolution.ofShortExact`: applied to the `n`-th cosyzygy short exact sequence with
   250	`P = I_A.X (n+1)`, `Q = I_C.X (n+1)`, it produces the monomorphism into the next biproduct term
   251	whose cokernel feeds the following stage. -/
   252	lemma mono_biprod_lift_factorThru_of_exact {S : ShortComplex 𝒜} (hS : S.Exact) [Mono S.f]
   253	    {P Q : 𝒜} [Injective P] (α : S.X₁ ⟶ P) [Mono α] (γ : S.X₃ ⟶ Q) [Mono γ] :
   254	    Mono (biprod.lift (Injective.factorThru α S.f) (S.g ≫ γ)) := by
   255	  rw [Preadditive.mono_iff_cancel_zero]
   256	  intro T x hx
   257	  have h1 : x ≫ Injective.factorThru α S.f = 0 := by simpa using hx =≫ biprod.fst
   258	  have h2 : x ≫ S.g ≫ γ = 0 := by simpa using hx =≫ biprod.snd
   259	  have hxg : x ≫ S.g = 0 := by rw [← cancel_mono γ, zero_comp, Category.assoc]; exact h2
   260	  have hyf : hS.lift x hxg ≫ S.f = x := hS.lift_f x hxg
   261	  have hya : hS.lift x hxg ≫ α = 0 := by
   262	    have h3 : hS.lift x hxg ≫ S.f ≫ Injective.factorThru α S.f = 0 := by
   263	      rw [← Category.assoc, hyf]; exact h1
   264	    rwa [Injective.comp_factorThru] at h3
   265	  have hy0 : hS.lift x hxg = 0 := by rw [← cancel_mono α, zero_comp]; exact hya

   268	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — twisted biproduct of cochain complexes
   269	
   270	This block builds the *structural* core of the dual Horseshoe Lemma as a general, injective-free
   271	construction. Given two cochain complexes `K`, `L` and a degreewise family
   272	`τ n : L.X n ⟶ K.X (n+1)` satisfying the cocycle identity
   273	`L.d n (n+1) ≫ τ (n+1) = -(τ n ≫ K.d (n+1) (n+2))`, the biproduct objects `K.X n ⊞ L.X n` with the
   274	twisted matrix differential `[[d_K, τ], [0, d_L]]` form a cochain complex `twistedBiprod τ hτ`,
   275	the coprojection `K ⟶ twistedBiprod` and projection `twistedBiprod ⟶ L` are chain maps, and every
   276	degree is the canonical split short exact sequence of the biproduct.
   277	
   278	This is exactly the content of the blueprint sub-lemmas `lem:horseshoe_dComp` (the differential
   279	squares to zero) and `lem:horseshoe_chainMap` (the coprojection/projection are chain maps and the
   280	degrees split); it is isolated here free of injectivity because the only inputs are the cocycle
   281	identity and the biproduct structure. The horseshoe specialises it to `K = I_A.cocomplex`,
   282	`L = I_C.cocomplex` once the twist `τ` has been produced by injectivity. -/

   293	    (K.X n ⊞ L.X n) ⟶ (K.X (n + 1) ⊞ L.X (n + 1)) :=
   294	  biprod.lift (biprod.fst ≫ K.d n (n + 1) + biprod.snd ≫ τ n) (biprod.snd ≫ L.d n (n + 1))
   295	
   296	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   297	lemma twistedBiprodD_fst (n : ℕ) :
   298	    twistedBiprodD τ n ≫ biprod.fst = biprod.fst ≫ K.d n (n + 1) + biprod.snd ≫ τ n := by

   303	    twistedBiprodD τ n ≫ biprod.snd = biprod.snd ≫ L.d n (n + 1) := by

615	/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — the augmented Čech complex on `X`
   616	
   617	The lemma `cechAugmented_exact` (`lem:cech_augmented_resolution`) asserts that the
   618	augmented {\v C}ech complex `0 → F → C⁰ → C¹ → ⋯` of a quasi-coherent sheaf `F`
   619	over an affine open cover `𝒰` is **exact** in `QCoh(X)` — i.e. the {\v C}ech nerve
   620	is a resolution of `F`. This is the *un-pushed* (over `X`, not relative to `f`)
   621	counterpart of `CechComplex`/`relativeCechComplexOfNerve`. We record here the
   622	structural ingredients that the exactness statement is phrased against: the
   623	un-augmented {\v C}ech complex on `X` (`cechComplexOnX`), obtained from the {\v C}ech
   624	nerve exactly as `relativeCechComplexOfNerve` does but with the *identity*
   625	pushforward — i.e. directly, with no `f_*`. -/
   626	
   627	/-- **The (un-augmented) {\v C}ech cochain complex of `F` on `X`.** This is the
   628	alternating-coface-map complex `C⁰ → C¹ → ⋯` of the underlying cosimplicial object
   629	of the {\v C}ech nerve `CechNerve 𝒰 F` (its augmentation `F` is dropped). It is the
   630	`f = 𝟙`/un-pushed analogue of `relativeCechComplexOfNerve`: the same coherence-free
   631	plumbing without the relative pushforward `f_*`, so it is the complex whose
   632	exactness (after re-adjoining the augmentation `F → C⁰`) is the content of

 11516	\begin{proof}
 11517	  \uses{def:cech_complex_on_X, def:cech_complex}
 11518	  The direct image \(f_*\) is an additive functor, so it commutes with the functor
 11519	  that assembles a cosimplicial module into its alternating-coface cochain complex.
 11520	  Concretely, in each degree \(p\) both complexes have the same object, the image
 11521	  \(f_*(\mathcal{C}^p)\) of the degree-\(p\) {\v C}ech term; the degree-\(p\)
 11522	  differential of the relative {\v C}ech complex is exactly the image under \(f_*\) of
 11523	  the degree-\(p\) differential of the complex on \(X\). The latter differential is
 11524	  the alternating sum \(\sum_{j} (-1)^j \delta_j\) of the cofaces \(\delta_j\), and
 11525	  additivity of \(f_*\) --- its preservation of finite sums, of integer scalar
 11526	  multiples and of negation --- gives
 11527	  \[
 11528	    f_*\Bigl(\sum_j (-1)^j \delta_j\Bigr)
 11529	      \;=\;
 11530	    \sum_j (-1)^j\, f_*(\delta_j).
 11531	  \]
 11532	  Assembling these degreewise data --- the identity on objects together with the
 11533	  commuting squares expressing the differential identities --- produces the asserted
 11534	  isomorphism of cochain complexes.
 11535	\end{proof}

events.text: I’m making the first Lean edit in the abstract homological-algebra module: two reusable facts extract positive-degree exactness and the degree-zero cycles isomorphism from any exact augmentation, and a new derived-functor comparison consumes that exact augmentation directly. This isolates all degree-shift normalization from the cover-indexed Čech terms.

The generic proofs themselves elaborate; the first LSP pass found only namespace projection errors in the wrapper and an unused inherited injective-resolution instance. I’m qualifying the helper calls explicitly and scoping out that irrelevant instance, which keeps the API genuinely more general.

521	\begin{definition}
   522	[Per-affine-open piece of the base-change iso]
   523	  \label{def:relspec_pullback_iso_affine_piece}
   524	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RelativeSpec.pullback_iso_affine_piece}
   525	  \uses{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}
   526	  For an affine open \(U \subseteq T\), the preimage \(q^{-1}(U)\) is affine and is
   527	  canonically isomorphic to \(\Spec\) of the sections of the pulled-back algebra
   528	  \(g^*\mathcal{A}\) over \(U\). This per-piece isomorphism feeds the global base-change
   529	  iso construction.
   530	\end{definition}
   531	
   532	\begin{proof}
   533	  As \(q\) is affine (\cref{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}), \(q^{-1}(U)\) is
   534	  affine; its canonical isomorphism with \(\Spec \Gamma(q^{-1}(U), \mathcal{O})\) matches
   535	  the sections of the pushforward \(g^*\mathcal{A}\) over \(U\) by definitional
   536	  unfolding. Constructed directly in Lean.
   537	\end{proof}

   539	\begin{definition}

   542	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RelativeSpec.pullback_cocone}
   543	  \uses{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}

   545	  pullback \(T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})\); its component at an affine
   546	  open \(U\) is the canonical map \(\Spec((g^*\mathcal{A})(U)) \to
   547	  T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})\) into the affine piece \(q^{-1}(U)\).
   548	\end{definition}

   551	  The components are the affine-open inclusion maps of the pulled-back pieces; their

   553	  restriction along basic opens. Constructed directly in Lean.

   563	  \(\underline{\Spec}_T(g^*\mathcal{A}) \to T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})\),
   564	  composed with the projection \(q\), equals the structure morphism
   565	  \(\underline{\Spec}_T(g^*\mathcal{A}) \to T\) of the relative spectrum of
   566	  \(g^*\mathcal{A}\).
   567	\end{lemma}

   696	  \(\underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{B}) \to \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})\) via the

   698	  representing bijection in \(\mathcal{A}\). For the equivalence claim, \(\underline{\Spec}_X\)

   707	  \(\Spec\Gamma(\pi^{-1}(U), \mathcal{O}_Y) \to \Spec\Gamma(\pi^{-1}(U), \mathcal{O}_Y)\)).

   710	\section{Lean encoding}
   711	\label{sec:relspec_lean_encoding}
   712	
   713	The Lean target file is the new \texttt{AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RelativeSpec.lean}.
   714	The construction proceeds by gluing absolute affine pieces: for each affine open
   715	\(U \subseteq X\) with \(U = \Spec R\) and \(A := \mathcal{A}(U)\) regarded as an
   716	\(R\)-algebra, the local piece is \(\Spec A\) with structure morphism \(\Spec A \to \Spec R = U\)
   717	induced by the algebra unit \(R \to A\). Mathlib provides \texttt{IsAffineOpen.toScheme} for
   718	the affine-open inclusion and the absolute \texttt{Scheme.Spec} functor for the local
   719	pieces; the transition isomorphisms come from quasi-coherence of \(\mathcal{A}\) via
   720	\texttt{QuasiCoherent.tensorIso} (or the explicit
   721	\(\mathcal{A}(U) \otimes_R S \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{A}(V)\) for \(V = \Spec S \subseteq U\)).
   722	The gluing backbone is \texttt{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData} (general construction) or
   723	the convenience wrapper \texttt{AlgebraicGeometry.AffineScheme.glueOpens}; the cocycle
   724	condition reduces to Stacks \texttt{lemma-transitive-spec}. The universal property
   725	(\cref{thm:relative_spec_univ}) is expressed as a
   726	\texttt{CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy} witness, providing the natural bijection
   727	$\Hom_X(T, \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})) \cong
   728	\Hom_{\mathcal{O}_X\text{-alg}}(\mathcal{A}, g_*\mathcal{O}_T)$ as a
   729	\texttt{Yoneda}-style structure. The base-change isomorphism
   730	(\cref{thm:relative_spec_base_change}) and functoriality
   731	(\cref{thm:relative_spec_functorial}) are derived from the universal property by
   732	Yoneda. No new core axiom is required; the entire chapter is a definitional/structural
   733	construction on top of existing Mathlib affine-scheme infrastructure.

   443	\section{Pullback compatibility helpers}
   444	\label{sec:relspec_pullback_helpers}
   445	
   446	This section records the substrate lemmas and constructions underlying the
   447	base-change isomorphism (\cref{thm:relative_spec_base_change}). Throughout,
   448	\(g : T \to X\) is a morphism of schemes, \(\mathcal{A}\) is a quasi-coherent
   449	\(\mathcal{O}_X\)-algebra, and \(q\) denotes the first projection of the pullback
   450	\(T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})\) along the structure morphism
   451	\(\pi : \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A}) \to X\). The pulled-back quasi-coherent
   452	\(\mathcal{O}_T\)-algebra \(g^*\mathcal{A}\) is realised as the pushforward
   453	\(q_* \mathcal{O}_{T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})}\).
   454	
   455	\begin{lemma}
   456	[Affineness of the structural pullback projection]
   457	  \label{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}
   458	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QcohAlgebra.pullback_fst_isAffineHom}
   459	  \uses{thm:relative_spec_univ, def:relspec_structure_morphism}
   460	  The first projection
   461	  \(q : T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A}) \to T\) of the pullback of the
   462	  structure morphism \(\pi\) along \(g\) is an affine morphism.
   463	\end{lemma}
   464	
   465	\begin{proof}
   466	  The structure morphism \(\pi\) is affine by \cref{thm:relative_spec_univ}, and
   467	  affineness of morphisms is stable under base change; hence its pullback \(q\) is
   468	  affine. Proved directly in Lean.
   469	\end{proof}
   470	
   471	\begin{lemma}
   472	[Quasi-coherence overlay for the pushforward along the affine projection]
   473	  \label{lem:relspec_pullback_coequifibered}
   474	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QcohAlgebra.pullback_coequifibered}
   475	  \uses{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}
   476	  The pushforward \(q_* \mathcal{O}_{T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})}\)
   477	  along the affine projection \(q\) carries the Stacks~01LL quasi-coherence overlay:
   478	  for every affine open \(U \subseteq T\) and section \(r \in \Gamma(T, U)\), the
   479	  restriction of the pushforward to the basic open \(D(r) \subseteq U\) is the
   480	  localization away from \(r\) of its sections over \(U\). This is the predicate making
   481	  \(g^*\mathcal{A}\) a well-formed quasi-coherent \(\mathcal{O}_T\)-algebra.
   482	\end{lemma}
   483	
   484	\begin{proof}
   485	  Since \(q\) is affine (\cref{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}), the preimage
   486	  \(q^{-1}(U)\) of an affine open \(U\) is affine, and \(q^{-1}(D(r))\) is the basic open
   487	  of \(q^{-1}(U)\) cut out by the pulled-back section; the localization-away
   488	  identification then follows from the affine-open localization criterion. Proved
   489	  directly in Lean.
   490	\end{proof}

   494	[Base change of a quasi-coherent algebra]
   495	  \label{def:relspec_qcoh_pullback}

   497	  \uses{def:qc_sheaf_of_algebras, lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom,
   498	    lem:relspec_pullback_coequifibered}
   499	  Let \(g : T \to X\) be a morphism of schemes and \(\mathcal{A}\) a quasi-coherent
   500	  \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-algebra (\cref{def:qc_sheaf_of_algebras}). The \emph{base change}
   501	  (pullback) \(g^*\mathcal{A}\) of \(\mathcal{A}\) along \(g\) is the quasi-coherent
   502	  \(\mathcal{O}_T\)-algebra realised as the pushforward
   503	  \(q_* \mathcal{O}_{T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A})}\) along the first
   504	  projection \(q : T \times_X \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A}) \to T\) of the pullback of
   505	  the structure morphism \(\pi\) along \(g\). Concretely, the underlying
   506	  \(\mathcal{O}_T\)-module is the topological pushforward \(q_* \mathcal{O}\) and the unit
   507	  is the comorphism \(q^\sharp : \mathcal{O}_T \to q_* \mathcal{O}\); the Stacks~01LL
   508	  quasi-coherence (coequifibered) overlay is supplied by
   509	  \cref{lem:relspec_pullback_coequifibered}, which itself rests on the affineness of \(q\)
   510	  (\cref{lem:relspec_pullback_fst_isaffinehom}). This is the project's base-change
   511	  constructor for quasi-coherent algebras, packaging \(g^*\mathcal{A}\) as a value of
   512	  \(\mathrm{QcohAlg}(T)\); it is the object underlying the base-change isomorphism
   513	  (\cref{thm:relative_spec_base_change}).
   514	\end{definition}
